 Advertisement Advertisement MMA MMA News Costa Pitches Backup Role For Van vs. Kape
 Tom Rashid UFC & MMA Lead Writer · 21 November 2026 Alessandro Costa rematches Amir Albazi at UFC Qatar on Saturday, hunting a fourth finish in 2026 and revenge for a knockout loss four years ago.
 The Brazilian flyweight plans to rest his body after an intense stretch—three stoppages across 99 days from April through July, beating Stewart Nicoll, Matt Schnell and Cody Durden before the third round each time—but told MMA Fighting he would make an exception if the UFC needs a replacement for the January title bout in Toronto. Joshua Van defends against Manel Kape at UFC 336 on Jan. 30, and Costa wants to stay ready in case either man pulls out.
 Costa's Path To A UFC Flyweight Title Shot
 "My dream comes first," Costa said in the interview. He added that he would let the promotion know he remains available even while recovering.
 Costa sits outside the rankings but believes the current flyweight landscape offers openings. The winner of Kyoji Horiguchi and Asu Almabayev, who also fight Saturday in Doha, gains the clearest path forward. Costa argued that weight-cutting issues or last-minute injuries could create gaps for unranked contenders under the UFC's current approach to matchmaking.
 The rematch with Albazi holds personal weight. Costa accepted their first meeting on nine days' notice while battling undisclosed health problems, losing his octagon debut in 2022. He now carries three straight wins against an opponent coming off back-to-back defeats and feels the experience gap has closed.
 Costa wants a top-10 opponent next if he finishes Albazi and closes what he describes as the best year of his career with four stoppages across eight months.
